author: bumbosiepsak
title: Windows CC build fails with MSBuild worker StackOverflowException during benchmark_app compilation
signature: Windows CC build fails - an MSBuild worker process crashes with a .NET StackOverflowException during parallel compilation (benchmark_app / samples build), causing CMake Generator error: execution of make failed|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Conditional Compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: MSBuild aborts building samples/cpp/benchmark_app/benchmark_app.vcxproj: an MSBuild worker process logs 'Process is terminated due to StackOverflowException.' and 'Stack overflow', then CMake reports 'Generator: execution of make failed'

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status job reports failure because the Conditional Compilation build job failed

key_errors: Process is terminated due to StackOverflowException.

CMake Error: Generator: execution of make failed. Make command was: C:/BuildTools/MSBuild/Current/Bin/amd64/MSBuild.exe samples/cpp/benchmark_app/benchmark_app.vcxproj /p:Configuration=Release /p:Platform=x64 /p:VisualStudioVersion=17.0 /m:15 /v:m /verbosity:minimal
root_cause: During the final stage of the Windows CC build (linking/building samples/cpp/benchmark_app with MSBuild running 15 parallel worker nodes, /CGTHREADS:15), one of the MSBuild worker (MSBuild.exe node) processes crashed with a .NET StackOverflowException, which is an unrecoverable CLR-level crash that immediately kills the worker process rather than raising a normal compiler/linker diagnostic. No compiler error (e.g., C1060, LNK1102) precedes it, unlike the previously-tracked 'out of heap space under high parallelism' pattern (signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e, 21 occurrences) - this is a distinct failure mode: an MSBuild host/node process itself is crashing, not cl.exe running out of heap. This points to resource exhaustion (likely native stack or memory pressure on the MSBuild.exe process, exacerbated by high parallelism of 15 concurrent compile/link jobs) on the same memory-constrained self-hosted Windows CC runner class responsible for the recurring C1060 pattern, rather than a code defect in the merged PR (#39961, a revert reinstating the Protobuf 6.31.1 bump, touching only build/dependency files, not benchmark_app or MSBuild invocation logic).
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI; requires the same Windows runner resource constraints and MSBuild node crash conditions. Locally: build the CC (SELECTIVE_BUILD=COLLECT -> ON) configuration with MSVC under constrained RAM and a high /m (MSBuild node count, e.g. /m:15) targeting samples/cpp/benchmark_app, while the rest of the tree is also compiling in parallel, to approximate resource exhaustion in an MSBuild worker process.
recommended_actions: Reduce MSBuild parallelism (/m:<N>, currently 15) for the Windows CC job to lower concurrent MSBuild.exe worker memory/stack pressure.

Investigate whether the self-hosted Windows CC runner pool is resource-constrained (RAM/CPU) relative to the parallelism configured in windows_conditional_compilation.yml, consistent with the already-tracked C1060 pattern (signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e).

If this StackOverflowException recurs, capture a crash dump of the MSBuild node process (enable Windows Error Reporting / procdump on the runner) to identify which task triggers the native/managed stack overflow.

Escalate to CI infra team alongside the existing Windows CC resource-exhaustion ticket since both symptoms (C1060 and MSBuild worker StackOverflowException) likely share the same root infrastructure constraint (runner memory/CPU sizing vs configured parallelism).
prevention_strategies: Cap MSBuild node/thread parallelism on memory-constrained Windows CC runners, and add a rerun-once-with-reduced-parallelism self-healing step if a StackOverflowException or C1060 is detected in the log, since these are transient infra-driven failures unrelated to code correctness.
historical_context: The Windows CC job has a well-established recurring 'out of heap space' MSVC resource-exhaustion pattern (signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e, 21 occurrences since 2026-11-03, most recently 2026-11-23T13:22:55Z) and a related 'build job cancelled mid-compilation' pattern (signature_hash 73496f939a352d74, 1 occurrence). This run's failure - an MSBuild worker crashing with .NET StackOverflowException rather than a compiler C1060/LNK1102 error - has not been seen before in this database and is recorded here as a new, closely related pattern under the same Infrastructure category and likely root cause (Windows CC runner resource constraints under high build parallelism).
